_about: Commons File:BAe 146 v1.0.png (Julien.scavini, CC BY-SA 3.0): an enthusiast's dimensioned side, plan, front and section schematic of the BAe 146 (1355 x 830 px), flattened onto white (its background is transparent) and saved at 72 dpi so pymupdf opens it at 1 pt a pixel. The side view: layers.py --mode image --threshold 170 at scale 4 (4 raster px per scan px), clip 15,5,710,200, --xscale 0.9148 (the side and plan are drawn 9.3% long lengthwise against their own span, height and scale bar: evened out, see recipe.json). Pixels of that raster, line centres. The crown is hidden under the wing's root fairing from 6.3 m to 16.2 m (bridged level). The belly is hidden behind the main gear's fairing (bridged). The top line from the wing to the fin is the dorsal fillet (fin.fillet); the fuselage's own crown runs under it down to the tail cone, whose end is the clamshell airbrake's (a blunt end, 0.7 m tall). The inboard nacelle's aft part is hidden behind the outboard one: its hidden lines are the outboard's profile moved 68 px forward and 10 px up (free points).
